style_context: Wilderness survival skills including shelter building, fire starting, first aid, water treatment, signaling for rescue, and outdoor emergency preparedness

images.description: Scout sitting inside a completed natural shelter made from branches and leaves, looking prepared and calm
Visual ranking of the five priorities of wilderness survival with icons showing the order and brief description of each

Grid showing common backcountry hazards: a thunderstorm over mountains, a coiled rattlesnake, a swollen river crossing, a steep rocky trail with loose scree, and a dense fog-covered forest, each scene clearly labeled
All 10 Scout Essentials laid out on a backpack, each item clearly visible and organized in order
Completed trip plan form showing route on map, participant list, timeline, emergency contacts, and weather forecast
Pyramid diagram with the seven survival priorities stacked from bottom to top, each level showing priority number, name, and survival timeframe
Left side showing a panicked Scout making poor decisions with arrows pointing to negative outcomes, right side showing calm Scout making good decisions with positive outcomes
Well-organized first aid kit in waterproof pouch with compartments showing bandages, medications, tools, and items clearly visible
Five different shelter setups arranged side-by-side, each labeled with condition (cold and snowy, wet, hot and dry, windy, at water) showing appropriate shelter design for each
Three columns showing clothing layers for cold weather, hot weather, and wet weather conditions, each column displaying layered outfit from base to shell

Four types of hiking footwear side-by-side: lightweight trail runners for dry trails, waterproof hiking boots for wet terrain, insulated winter boots for snow, and sandals crossed out with an X for wilderness survival
Top-down view of properly organized campsite showing sleeping area, cooking area, food storage location with distances marked, and bear/raccoon protection measures

Two food storage methods side-by-side: a bear canister sitting on the ground next to a tree, and a bear hang with a stuff sack suspended from a rope over a high tree branch, each labeled with pros and cons
Three forest shelter types displayed side-by-side: lean-to shelter, debris shelter (A-frame), and natural shelter with rock overhang, each labeled with construction details

Cross-section cutaway diagram of a snow cave showing the entrance tunnel angled downward, the raised sleeping platform above the entrance level, a ventilation hole in the ceiling, and smooth domed interior walls
Scout actively building a debris shelter, showing the framework of branches leaning against a ridgepole and bundles of leaves and insulation nearby
Interior view looking into a completed debris shelter showing a thick layer of dry leaves and pine needles as bedding on the ground, with daylight filtering through gaps in the branch walls
Scout demonstrating proper ferro rod striking technique over a prepared tinder bundle, showing the correct striking angle and spark generation

Three stages of building a fire shown left to right: first a small tinder bundle with glowing ember, then thin kindling sticks arranged in a teepee shape over flames, then a mature campfire with larger fuel logs burning steadily
Aerial view showing five large ground-to-air signals (X, V, arrow, F, checkmark) each properly arranged and labeled, visible from above as they would appear to aircraft
Simple diagram showing three whistle signal patterns: one blast means stop, two blasts means come to me, three blasts means emergency help needed, each pattern shown as sound wave icons with a label
Top-down view showing sun position, mirror angle, and target alignment for proper signal mirror technique with angles and light path clearly marked

Several improvised signaling devices arranged on a rock: a polished aluminum can bottom reflecting sunlight, a CD disc catching light, a glass lens, and a piece of shiny metal, all glistening in bright daylight
A signal fire on a hilltop clearing producing a tall thick column of white smoke rising high into a clear blue sky, with green pine branches piled next to the fire for smoke generation

Bird's-eye view showing a large X signal on open ground made from dark logs, with measurement markers showing the signal is at least 10 feet across, surrounded by contrasting lighter terrain for maximum visibility from the air
Three water treatment methods displayed side-by-side: boiling with pot and fire, purification tablets in water, and filter pump with labeled steps for each method

Two clear water bottles held side-by-side in bright sunlight: left bottle contains cloudy brownish water scooped from a stream, right bottle contains crystal clear filtered water, dramatic visual contrast
Grid showing five common edible plants with detailed illustrations of leaves, flowers, roots, and growth patterns, each plant clearly labeled with name and edible parts highlighted

Detailed botanical illustration showing two plants side-by-side: a dandelion with bright yellow flower, jagged leaves, and long taproot, and a cattail with tall brown seedhead, long flat leaves, and thick rhizome, edible parts highlighted in green
Five signaling tools arranged together: cell phone, personal locator beacon, whistle, signal mirror, and flashlight, each clearly visible and labeled

Simple horizontal bar chart showing effective range of different signaling methods: personal locator beacon reaches worldwide, signal mirror visible up to 10 miles, signal fire visible up to 5 miles, whistle audible up to 1 mile, voice carries a few hundred yards
Modern search and rescue coordination center with personnel working at desks with maps, radios, and technology coordinating rescue operations
